list: The official 55 trophies, as published for PlayStation 5 (list went public 18 November 2026, ahead of the 19 November 2026 launch)
listNote: Names, descriptions and grades are shown exactly as PlayStation publishes them, via Exophase and PSNProfiles. Counts (stunts, locations, spots) are the progress targets PlayStation tracks, as listed by PSNProfiles. Every guide below is written for this entry in our own words; where no published walkthrough pins down a location or step yet, the guide says so instead of inventing one.

pushsquare.label: Push Square — GTA 6 PS5 Trophies Revealed, 100% Completion Needed for the Platinum (18 Nov 2026)

trophies.guide: The platinum pops the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned — there is nothing extra to do for it. Work the roadmap in order: story first, then activities and collectibles, then the long counters, and finish with the 100% completion gold, which is the last gate for most players. Budget a long grind: early coverage puts the platinum at roughly 200 hours, and the list has no difficulty trophy, so it is long rather than hard.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

trophies.guide: Finish the opening mission, Gone Fishing. It is the first story trophy and cannot be skipped — just play the story from the start. Because it is tied to one story moment, keep a manual save before you begin the mission: early guides report GTA VI has no mission replay, so a missed story beat cannot be redone from a menu (that claim is still unconfirmed).
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

trophies.guide: Play through Chapter 1 to its end; the trophy pops when the chapter closes. Chapters are the story's big beats, so there is no shortcut — finish every mission the chapter gives you. Keep a manual save at the start of the chapter in case a story moment inside it turns out to be missable.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost

trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 2. This is where the second protagonist becomes playable, which opens up most of the open-world activities — so clear the chapter before you sink time into side content. As with every chapter trophy, keep a manual save at the chapter's start until mission replay is confirmed either way.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

trophies.guide: Play Chapter 3 through to its end. By now the robbery side of the game opens up — several activity trophies (bank vaults, armored trucks, illegal operations) become available around this point in the story, so it pays to finish the chapter before grinding them. Manual save at the chapter start, as for the other chapter trophies.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!

trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 4, the last full chapter before the finale. Once it closes, mop up any story-moment trophies you have not earned yet before you take the final mission — the finale is the last story beat, and anything tied to a chapter you have left behind may not come back.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma

trophies.guide: Finish the final mission to earn this gold. Before you start it, make a manual save: it is the last story mission, and early guides report there is no mission replay and no New Game Plus, so anything you have not done in the story is best done before this point (unconfirmed — treat the save as cheap insurance). After the finale, the open world stays open for cleanup.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run. Mission trophies pop on completion, whatever your performance — there is no medal requirement on this list, so play it however you like. Keep a manual save before the mission, as with all story-moment trophies.
trophies.name: Trust

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist. It is one of the story's set-piece heists — finish the mission and the trophy is yours. No published walkthrough pins down any extra step inside the mission yet, so just complete it; if a step inside it ever proves missable, the linked guides will say so.
trophies.name: Break the Bank

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play. Like the other mission trophies it is awarded for finishing the mission, with no score or style condition in the official description. Save before the mission as a precaution against the reported lack of mission replay.
trophies.name: Family Matters

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. The name suggests a show or performance set piece; the official description asks only for completion, so finish the mission and move on. Keep your chapter-start manual save current.
trophies.name: DWNFALL

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown, set at Vice City International Airport. Finishing the mission is the whole requirement. The airport also matters for the Catch Me If You Can trophy, so while you are in the area, keep that one in mind — but it is a separate, free-roam trophy, not part of this mission.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory. The official description asks only for completion — no extra objective is listed. It is a late-story mission trophy, so by the time you reach it you should already have your manual saves in place for the finale.
trophies.name: Snow Storm

trophies.guide: Reach 100% on the game's own completion checklist — the same requirement Rockstar has used since GTA III, and the last gate before the platinum for most players. It does not mean doing literally everything in Leonida: the in-game checklist (story, stranger strands, collectibles, activities and challenges) is what counts, and early coverage notes the 35-task checklist behind it. Work it last, after the story and the big counters, and use the checklist in this guide to track what is left.
trophies.name: A Long Road

trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts across Leonida — jumps, airtime, near misses and the like, as the game counts them. This is a pure grind trophy: work on it whenever you are driving between missions rather than in one sitting, and let the total build up naturally. PlayStation tracks the count for you, so check your progress on the trophy itself. No location is pinned down yet — any stunt anywhere counts.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Sample every activity type the game offers — racing, fishing, shooting range, arcade, bowling, drone racing, meditation, hunting and the rest — one try each. The official description says 'each type', and PSN tracks 9 of them. Work through the list in this guide one by one; the activities all unlock during the story, so do this after Chapter 2 when both protagonists are playable. Nothing here needs winning, only trying.
trophies.name: Master of None

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Gold-medal all 42 Shooting Range challenges. This is the list's first real skill gate: a silver that asks for golds across every challenge. Practice one weapon class at a time, learn each challenge's par, and expect to repeat the hard ones — there is no shortcut in the official description. The range is a repeatable activity, so nothing here can be missed; it just takes aim and patience.
trophies.name: The Shootist

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations. Each location is its own race, so you must win — not just enter — at every one of them. Learn each course's line before you race it for the win, and treat the easier locations first to learn how the drones handle. Locations are spread across Leonida, so this doubles as a tour of the map.
trophies.name: Top Fun

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — different events, not the same race 20 times. Mix street races, drone races and whatever other race types the game offers, and count each new event you win. Losing a race costs nothing but time, and every race type is repeatable, so work through the race list across free roam after the story opens the map up.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Fishing is one of the game's side activities — find Cal, take his challenge, and out-fish him. The official description names a person, not a place, so no location is pinned down yet; check the linked trophy lists and early guides for where Cal's challenge triggers once players report it. Losing just means trying again.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle

trophies.guide: Finish one full arcade game at an arcade. Any game counts — pick the one you enjoy most and play it to its end. Arcades are open-world locations, so this is a quick trophy once you find one; no score or difficulty condition is listed in the official description.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Finish Andy's stranger mission strand — the last mission in his chain. Stranger strands unlock across Leonida as you explore, and each one ends with a final mission that carries its own trophy. Find Andy's strand, play it to its end, and this pops. Stranger missions are open-world content, so they stay available after the story; the missable risk is only if a strand is tied to a story chapter, which is not stated — play them as you find them.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Finish Kenton's stranger mission strand with its final mission. Same pattern as the other stranger trophies: find the strand in the open world, play its missions in order, and the trophy pops on the last one. Do the strands as you meet them rather than leaving them all to the end, so nothing is left riding on a chapter you have already passed.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's stranger mission strand with its final mission. Billy's chain is one of five named stranger strands with its own trophy, and all five count toward the Strangers & Freaks silver as well — so every strand you finish pulls double duty toward that trophy too.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Finish 8 full stranger mission strands across Leonida. Five of them have their own trophies (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone), so those five are your foundation — find three more strands beyond them. Strangers appear as you explore the map, so wander: the strands are the game's way of rewarding curiosity. Keep count in this guide's tracker; PSN tracks the total for you.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Finish Randy's stranger mission strand with its final mission. Randy is one of the five named strangers with a dedicated trophy, and his strand counts toward the 8-strand silver. Play the strand as you find it in the open world.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's stranger mission strand with its final mission. Like the other named strangers, his chain ends in a trophy and counts toward Strangers & Freaks. No location is published for his strand yet — the linked trophy lists are the place to check once players report where each stranger appears.
trophies.name: Spin On This!

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 spots across Leonida. Meditation spots are quiet places scattered over the map — one early guide reports a spot on Lucia's balcony in Chapter 1 that disappears after that chapter, so do not leave this to the end: meditate at every spot you find, as soon as you find it, and keep a manual save at the start of each chapter (that disappearance claim is from one early guide and is still unconfirmed). The counter is tracked by PlayStation.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt the unique animal Bret asks for. Hunting is one of the game's activities — find Bret, take the hunt, and track the animal down. The official description names a person and a unique animal, not a place, so no location is pinned down yet; check the linked lists once players report where Bret's hunt takes place. The animal is unique, so this is a one-off hunt rather than a grind.
trophies.name: Fair Game

trophies.guide: Complete 3 full sets of collectible cards. Cards are hidden around Leonida — collect them, and a set completes when you hold every card in it. This is the list's pure collectible grind: work it with a map and a checklist, and use this guide's counter to track sets as they complete. No card locations are published in a verified walkthrough yet, so the linked trophy lists are the first place to look once players map them.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck

trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK feature at 100 different locations. WAiNK is the game's in-world photo or check-in style feature (its exact form is not described in the official text), and the count is tracked by PlayStation — so just keep using it wherever you go and let the total climb. This is a long grind best done passively: WAiNK at every new place you visit instead of saving it for a dedicated session.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

trophies.guide: Finish 50 of the game's challenges. Challenges are the small objectives layered over free roam — driving, shooting, exploration and more — and they stack up naturally as you play. Check the in-game challenge list regularly and chase the ones closest to done; the count is tracked by PlayStation, so this trophy is a matter of breadth, not one hard task.
trophies.name: One Last Thing

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, build a 4-star wanted level, then lose the cops and escape. Do it in open country or on the water where you can break line of sight, and keep your partner close — the trophy needs them with you when the heat drops. If the stars fall while you are alone, it does not count, so set it up deliberately rather than hoping it happens by accident.
trophies.name: Hot Together

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: With your partner, rob three shops in a row without ever losing your wanted level — the chain breaks if the heat drops between robberies. Pick three shops close together, plan the route, and keep moving: the wanted level has to stay live across all three. Do it in a quiet part of the map where the police response is slow.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy

trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles. Just driving past or getting into a new vehicle counts it as discovered, and Leonida is full of them — cars, bikes, boats, planes and more. Wander, try everything you see, and the total climbs on its own; PlayStation tracks the count. This is a passive trophy — do not grind it, let it happen while you explore.
trophies.name: Whip It Good

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Down 5 enemies during one use of Combat Focus, the game's slow-time aiming mode. Set it up where enemies cluster — a gang shootout or a police standoff — trigger Combat Focus, and drop five before it ends. If you only get three or four, just try again; the mode is repeatable and the trophy needs a single use, not a single mission.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Leave Vice City International Airport in an unscheduled way — in plain terms, steal a plane and take off without a flight plan. Get to the airfield, grab a plane, and get airborne; the trophy is about the departure, not the destination. Expect the airport to be guarded, so go in with a plan and a fast plane in mind.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can

trophies.guide: The official description is a joke, not an instruction: 'Kinda hot in these Rhinos.' Rhinos are the game's tanks, so this trophy involves them — most likely stealing one, driving one, or surviving one. No published walkthrough confirms the exact trigger yet, so treat it as a tank trophy: find a Rhino in the open world (military areas are the obvious place to look), get in it, and see what pops. Check the linked lists once players report the trigger.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store and get away without ever being detected. This is a stealth job: case the store, go in quiet, take the goods and leave before anyone raises the alarm. If you are spotted, the attempt fails — back out and try again rather than shooting your way out, since detection is what the trophy forbids. No store location is published yet; check the linked lists once players report one.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape after each one. Bank vaults are the big robbery targets — plan each hit, get in, take the vault, and get clean away, five times over. Escaping matters: a vault robbed but not escaped does not count. These unlock as the story's robbery side opens up, so work them from Chapter 3 onward.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks roam the roads — hit one, take its cargo, and get away clean. One truck is enough, but the escape is part of the requirement, so do not celebrate at the robbery: lose the heat first, then the trophy pops.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play

trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida. Just visiting each area counts — drive, fly and sail the whole map, and the trophy pops when the last area is ticked off. The in-game map shows what you have seen, so use it to find the gaps: islands, swamps and the far corners of the state are the ones players usually leave to last. This pairs naturally with the collectible hunts, so do them together.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob one illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs. Gangs run operations across Leonida — find one per gang, hit it, and move on to the next. The count is tracked by PlayStation, so keep a note of which gangs you have done; this guide's counter is the place for it. Operations are repeatable targets, so nothing here can be missed.
trophies.name: Pest Control

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Have a cocktail somewhere with a view on Ocean Beach. The official description gives you the place — Ocean Beach — and the act — a cocktail with a view — so find a bar or spot overlooking the beach, order or enjoy a drink there, and the trophy should pop. No exact venue is published yet; check the linked lists once players report the spot. This is a flavor trophy: slow down and enjoy it.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Drive a vehicle out of a showroom by smashing through it — 'in classic style', which is the game's way of saying do it loud and through the glass. Find a vehicle showroom, get in a car inside it, and drive straight out through the front. No showroom is named in the official description, so check the linked lists once players report one that works.
trophies.name: Capital Offense

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Play bowling at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley — and follow through, which suggests finishing a game there rather than just showing up. The official description names the venue, so find the Kolt & Associates alley, bowl a game, and the trophy pops on completion. Bowling is also one of the activity types for Master of None, so this pulls double duty.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling

trophies.guide: The official description is deliberately vague: 'A partnership with mass appeal.' No published walkthrough confirms the trigger yet — it reads like a social-media or fame moment for the two protagonists as a pair, so the likely shape is doing something together that gets noticed in the game's world. Do not chase this one blindly: play the story and the partner activities, and check the linked trophy lists once players report what actually triggers it.
trophies.name: Personal Best

trophies.guide: Make choices — 500 of them, as PlayStation tracks the count. This is the game's decision counter: dialogue choices, approach choices, and the small either-or moments of missions and free roam all feed it. There is no right answer to chase; just keep playing and choosing, and the total climbs. It is a long passive counter, so do not grind it — let it accumulate across the whole playthrough.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder

trophies.guide: The official description is a riddle: 'Second time's the charm.' No published walkthrough confirms the trigger yet, but the plain reading is succeeding at something on a second attempt — retrying a failed activity, race or challenge and winning it. If you fail something, try it once more straight away rather than walking off: the retry itself may be the trigger. Check the linked lists once players report the exact condition.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess

trophies.guide: The official description is a reaction, not an instruction: 'What the hell just happened?' That points at a scripted surprise or an easter egg — something strange that happens to you in the world rather than something you set out to do. No published walkthrough pins it down yet. Play the story and explore the odd corners of Leonida, and when something weird happens, this is probably the trophy for it; check the linked lists once players report the trigger.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone over with a melee drive-by — that is, hit someone with a melee weapon while driving past. Get a vehicle, get a melee weapon ready, and drive by a pedestrian target at speed. It is a deliberately silly trophy: one clean hit is all it takes, and it is repeatable until it lands.
trophies.name: Ten Pin

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 of Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills come from robberies — bank vaults, armored trucks and the like — and your contacts turn them into clean money. Keep robbing and keep laundering, and the total builds; the count is tracked by PlayStation. This pairs naturally with Maximum Withdrawal and the robbery trophies, so launder after every hit instead of letting bills pile up.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. Weapons, clothes, vehicles, food — every shop purchase counts toward the total, and it accumulates across the whole playthrough. Do not force it early: by the time you have bought the garages for Little Boxes and kitted yourself out, you will be most of the way there. PlayStation tracks the spend.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self

trophies.guide: Buy all 8 garage properties. Garages are the property purchases that also give you somewhere to store the vehicles you collect — so this trophy and Whip It Good feed each other. Properties unlock as the story progresses and money comes in; buy each garage as it becomes available rather than saving them all for the end, and keep the $100,000 spend of Treat Yo Self in mind as you pay for them.
trophies.name: Little Boxes

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Find vehicles in the world, bring them into the app's system, and register them — ten in total. It pairs with discovering vehicles for Whip It Good: every new vehicle you find is a candidate to register. The count is tracked by PlayStation, so work through the list as you explore.
trophies.name: On the Spot
